sentences.text:
Shri Sourabh Bhushan Shrivastava - Advocate for petitioner
 Shri Pramod Pandey - Government Advocate for State.

Order 
This is the third application filed under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 on behalf of applicant in connection with Crime No.146/2022, registered at Police Station-Govindpura,
District Bhopal (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) and 376(3) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
2. Learned counsel appearing for applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case, as he reviewed prosecutrix for talking to boys.
It is further submitted that applicant is in jail for long time.
There is no likelihood of completion of trial in near future.
Only two witnesses have been examined in the case.
There are total 25 witnesses in the case.
In these circumstances, applicant may be enlarged on bail.

3. Learned Government Advocate appearing for State opposed the bail NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:55464 2 MCRC-44921-2024 application.

It is submitted that prosecutrix is minor,
aged about 15 years.
She is step daughter of applicant.
There is direct allegations of rape against the applicant.
In these circumstances, applicant may not be released on bail.
4. First bail application filed by applicant was dismissed as withdrawn on 20.01.2023.

Thereafter,

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: is not concluded within a period of six months.
It is submitted that there is inordinate delay on part of prosecution.
Applicant cannot be kept in jail, as he is under trial prisoner, for long when there is delay on part of prosecution.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
6. On going through status report, which is available on record, it is found that only two witnesses have been examined i.e. on 25.07.2022 and thereafter, on 21.04.2023.
Court has stated that delay is not attributable to Court.
On going through the report, it is found that Court was not available after 13.08.2024.
Applicant was arrested on 24.03.2022.
He is in jail for about more than two and half years.
He is an old man aged about 60 years.
Trial is likely to take some more time for completion.
7. Considering the delay on part of prosecution, bail application filed by applicant is allowed.

It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court.

8 . The applicant shall also abide by the following conditions of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:55464 3 MCRC-44921-2024 Section 480 (3) of B.N.S.S. as under:-
(a) that such person shall attend in accordance with the conditions of the bond executed under this Chapter;
(b) that such person shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which the is accused, or suspected of the commission of which they are suspected and;
(c) that such person shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
9. C.C. as per rules (VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE vkt Suresh Malviya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42594412/
